label: General advertising law (applies to every category)

source.title: Consumer Protection Act 1999 (Act 599, incl. 2019 amendments) Parts II and IV; Food Act 1983 s.17; MAB Guideline Part 4 general principles

principles.principle: Advertising must not be misleading or deceptive, or likely to mislead or deceive the public, about the nature, manufacturing process, characteristics, suitability for a purpose, availability or quantity of goods.

No false or misleading representation that goods are of a particular kind, standard, quality, grade, quantity or composition, or that goods or services have any sponsorship, approval, endorsement, performance characteristics, uses or benefits. Falsely claiming a person has sponsorship, approval, endorsement or affiliation (e.g. 'approved by KKM' without approval) is also prohibited.

Representations made in an advertisement are deemed made by the person who claims to supply the goods, and/or the person on whose behalf the advertisement is made - a brand is presumed responsible for what its agency, distributor or influencer publishes for it, unless the contrary is proved.

Penalty exposure: a body corporate can be fined up to RM250,000 (RM500,000 for a second or subsequent offence); an individual up to RM100,000 or 3 years' imprisonment or both (up to RM250,000 or 6 years for repeat offences); plus up to RM1,000 for each day an offence continues after conviction.

All claims about objectively verifiable facts must be capable of substantiation; do not exploit the public's lack of knowledge with data they cannot verify. Absolute statements such as 'guaranteed', '100%' or 'no side effects' are high-risk unless substantiated or expressly permitted.
principles.regulation_reference: MAB Guideline §4.10, Appendix 3; Food Regulations 1985 reg 18(6)(c); NPRA Cosmetic Claims Guideline 'Other claims' (iv)

principles.principle: Food advertisements must carry the advertiser's true name and address (except oral or light/sound advertisements).
